answer: Agents cannot earn influence merely by creating identities: require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. A Sybil attacker must fund every identity separately and risks losing the capital, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free. Audits should sample claims across the horizon of activity, not just at entry; an onyx token or an ocean of new accounts cannot replace the bonded stake.
